title: GeoMER: A Joint Euclidean-Hyperbolic Geometry Framework for Multimodal Emotion Recognition
abstract: arXiv:2610.18587v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multimodal Emotion Recognition (MER) aims to understand human emotions by integrating information from multiple modalities such as speech and text. Psychological studies suggest that emotions exhibit latent hierarchical structured relationships in their semantic representations. However, most MER approaches rely on Euclidean representations, which capture fine-grained cross-modal interactions but do not explicitly provide a geometric prior for organizing hierarchical emotional structures. To mitigate this gap, we propose GeoMER, a joint Euclidean-Hyperbolic modeling framework that introduces hyperbolic emotion-core routing to capture higher-level, abstract emotional representations for MER. The proposed framework jointly models token-level cross-modal semantic interactions and latent emotion representations in two complementary geometric spaces. tldr: 提出GeoMER框架，将欧几里得与双曲几何相结合，通过双曲情感核心路由同时建模词元级跨模态语义交互与层次化情感结构，从而提升多模态情感识别性能。
en_tdlr: GeoMER, a joint Euclidean-Hyperbolic geometry framework, introduces hyperbolic emotion-core routing to jointly model token-level cross-modal semantic interactions and hierarchical emotional structures, improving multimodal emotion recognition.
